speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with a concerning rash and recent health changes; to help me diagnose your condition, could you please describe the appearance, location, and duration of the rash, as well as any other symptoms you are experiencing?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with a rash that started last night, finding it very concerning. He does not recall being exposed to any new environmental stimuli such as detergents or plants like poison ivy. He mentions he recently started seeing a primary care provider for arthritis management and a new onset cough.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) or Drug Eruption. The patient's history of recent arthritis management initiation, new onset cough, and acute rash suggests a systemic autoimmune flare or a hypersensitivity reaction to new medications. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP), and Antinuclear Antibody (ANA) titer. REQUEST IMAGES: Photos of the rash distribution.
